newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH buys Sephora for 1.6 bln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: LVMH buys Sephora for 1.6 bln Ffr.

text.p: LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton said on Wednesday that it had bought Sephora, France's leading perfume and beauty products retailer, for 1.6 billion francs ($260.8 million).
"LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton has acquired from the company's founders 100 percent of Sephora," it said in a statement.
"With this acquisition, LVMH becomes the world's leading distributor of perfumes and beauty products," it said.
LVMH earlier this year vastly expanded its presence in retailing with the $2.6 billion acquisition of San Francisco-based Duty Free Shoppers.

Sephora has 54 stores, including a new 14,000 square foot (1,300 square metre) shop on the prestigious Champs-Elysees. It generated 1996 sales of 1.37 billion francs, or eight percent of the French selective perfumes and beauty products market.

"Its prospects are outstanding, notably with the planned opening of 30 additional outlets in France over the next four years, as well as about 20 stores in other European markets and thanks to its development in Asia," the statement said.
